title: AI Trading's Alpha Singularity: Emergent Market Reasoning through Agent-to-Agent Self-Evolution
summary: Automated alpha mining holds the scoring function fixed and varies the search algorithm over it. A search that converges against a fixed scorer overfits whatever the scorer cannot penalize, a primary cause of the out-of-sample generalization gap. We treat the scoring function as a search artifact alongside the alpha factors and study what conditions make this joint search admissible. Sealed Joint Search (SJS) is a framework: a set of structural conditions on information flow in an autonomous-discovery system that prevent joint search from collapsing into self-confirmation while keeping the evaluator sealed. Conditions cover role decomposition, typed inter-role communication, provenance-sealed reads, versioned stores, and substrate-local promotion. Agora tests SJS empirically: five LLM agent classes communicate via three channels, evolving eight skill libraries, with alpha libraries built on AlphaGen operators. Three evaluators write reports aggregated into one brief, carrying forward disagreement instead of voting. We run Agora for 100 rounds on CSI 1000 and evaluate on a 91-day 2026 holdout sealed from all LLM inputs. Agora achieves holdout Sharpe +1.87; best baseline +1.334 at favorable seed and -0.755 cross-seed mean. Pre-loading Agora's two metrics into a frozen-library ablation recovers only +0.40 of the +2.25 Sharpe gap, and adding PPO without library evolution worsens the gap. The two metrics emerge rather than being designed. Caveats: single-seed run, short-side concentrated signal, intended for long-short.
core_methodology: Sealed Joint Search (SJS) framework with role decomposition, typed inter-role communication, provenance-sealed reads, versioned stores, and substrate-local promotion. Utilizes five LLM agent classes communicating via three channels to evolve eight skill libraries.
data_sources: CSI 1000 index with a 91-day holdout period in 2026, sealed from all LLM inputs.
alpha_potential: Achieves a holdout Sharpe ratio of +1.87, significantly outperforming baselines. The framework prevents overfitting and self-confirmation biases, leading to robust out-of-sample performance. The emergent metrics suggest potential for capturing unique market inefficiencies.
title_cn: AI交易的Alpha奇点：通过Agent-to-Agent自我进化实现的市场推理涌现
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种密封联合搜索（SJS）框架，通过五类LLM代理和三通道通信演化八个技能库，防止过拟合和自我确认偏差。在CSI 1000指数上，该框架在2026年91天的保留期内实现了+1.87的夏普比率，显著优于基线。该方法展示了在量化交易中利用多代理协作和进化算法挖掘Alpha的潜力。

title: Adaptive Financial Transformer with Regime-Gated Attention for Stock Return Prediction
summary: Adaptive Financial Transformer (AFT) is proposed for stock return prediction under non-stationary financial markets. The model incorporates a Market Regime Encoder, an Adaptive Gate Network, and an Adaptive Financial Context module to dynamically bias self-attention based on semantic relationships between financial indicators. Unlike conventional Transformer architectures that treat all input features uniformly, the proposed approach groups 95 engineered financial features into 11 semantic categories and adapts attention according to latent market regimes. The study also identifies and corrects sequence alignment and backtesting issues that can inflate reported trading performance, and introduces a financially-aware composite objective that jointly optimizes prediction error, directional accuracy, and non-overlapping Sharpe ratio. Extensive experiments compare the proposed architecture against classical machine learning models, recurrent neural networks, and Transformer baselines using chronological evaluation, five random seeds, ablation studies, hyperparameter optimization, explainability analysis, and multi-stock validation. Results demonstrate competitive predictive performance while reducing model complexity by 15.2% and improving parameter efficiency through feature selection, providing an interpretable Transformer architecture for financial time-series forecasting.
core_methodology: The paper proposes an Adaptive Financial Transformer (AFT) that incorporates a Market Regime Encoder, an Adaptive Gate Network, and an Adaptive Financial Context module to dynamically adjust self-attention based on semantic relationships between financial indicators. It groups 95 engineered financial features into 11 semantic categories and adapts attention according to latent market regimes. The study also addresses sequence alignment and backtesting issues and introduces a financially-aware composite objective.
data_sources: The paper likely uses historical stock market data with 95 engineered financial features, categorized into 11 semantic groups. Specific data sources are not mentioned but would typically include price, volume, and other market indicators.
alpha_potential: The model's ability to adapt to different market regimes and its focus on semantic relationships between financial indicators suggest potential for capturing regime-dependent inefficiencies. The composite objective optimizing prediction error, directional accuracy, and Sharpe ratio indicates a practical approach to generating actionable signals.
title_cn: 用于股票收益预测的具有 regime-gated attention 的自适应金融 Transformer
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种自适应金融 Transformer（AFT），通过市场状态编码器、自适应门网络和自适应金融上下文模块，动态调整基于金融指标语义关系的自注意力机制。模型将95个工程化金融特征分为11个语义类别，并根据潜在市场状态调整注意力。研究还解决了序列对齐和回测问题，并引入了一个金融感知的复合目标函数。实验表明，该模型在预测性能上具有竞争力，同时降低了模型复杂度并提高了参数效率，为金融时间序列预测提供了一种可解释的Transformer架构。

title: Persona-Trained Monte Carlo: Estimating Market-Outcome Distributions via Swarms of Persona-Conditioned Neural Policy Bots in a Limit Order Book
summary: We propose Persona-Trained Monte Carlo (PTMC), a method for estimating distributions of market-outcome statistics by repeatedly simulating limit-order-book interaction among swarms of persona-conditioned neural-policy trading bots. Each run instantiates many bots sharing one trained policy network but conditioned on heterogeneous, individually sampled persona parameters drawn from a learned trader-heterogeneity distribution; the bots interact in a continuous double auction, and the resulting price path is one Monte Carlo sample. Repeating this over independent persona-population draws yields an ensemble from which a target market statistic is estimated. Randomness enters through persona draws, within-run action sampling, and optional exogenous shocks, not solely through price as in classical Monte Carlo. We distinguish PTMC from adjacent paradigms, including classical Monte Carlo, hand-coded agent-based models, single-agent reinforcement learning, and large-language-model-based generative agents. To justify the design, we survey cross-disciplinary foundations -- agent-based computational economics, market microstructure, behavioral finance, deep reinforcement learning, generative/LLM-based agents, news-driven trading, systemic risk, econophysics, and game theory -- connecting each literature to a specific design choice in the policy network, training data, or validation protocol. We formalize the PTMC estimator and its convergence properties, specify a candidate bot architecture and training objective, and propose a four-level validation methodology: stylized-fact matching, microstructure- and agent-level checks, and historical stress-test comparison against a zero-intelligence baseline. The framework is proposed but not implemented: we contribute a formal estimator, a cross-disciplinary design justification, and a validation roadmap, and conclude with open research questions.
core_methodology: Persona-Trained Monte Carlo (PTMC) method for estimating market-outcome distributions using swarms of persona-conditioned neural-policy trading bots in a limit order book. The approach involves simulating interactions among heterogeneous trading bots conditioned on sampled persona parameters, with results aggregated over multiple Monte Carlo runs.
data_sources: Limit order book data, simulated trading interactions, and optionally exogenous shocks.
alpha_potential: The method provides a novel way to model and predict market outcomes by incorporating heterogeneous trader behaviors and interactions, which can uncover hidden patterns or inefficiencies in market microstructure. This could be valuable for developing trading strategies that exploit these dynamics.
title_cn: 人格训练的蒙特卡洛方法：通过限价订单簿中人格条件神经策略机器人群估计市场结果分布
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种人格训练的蒙特卡洛（PTMC）方法，通过模拟限价订单簿中人格条件神经策略机器人群的交互来估计市场结果分布。该方法结合了异质交易者行为和蒙特卡洛模拟，为市场微观结构分析和交易策略开发提供了新的工具。潜在应用包括高频交易、市场流动性预测和系统性风险评估。

title: Fast Numbers, Slow Language: Bridging Quantitative and Qualitative Earnings Signals
summary: Earnings announcements release two types of information sequentially: quantitative surprise (numeric earnings-per-share (EPS)/revenue versus analyst estimate) arrives first in press releases and financial news, processed by algorithmic traders within minutes; qualitative language (management tone, guidance, question-and-answer (Q&A) credibility) arrives 30-90 min later in the earnings conference call transcript (ECT), requiring human interpretation overnight. Financial economists have studied quantitative surprise for 50 years; natural language processing (NLP) researchers have studied qualitative ECT signals for a decade. Despite studying the same event, the two communities used incompatible frameworks: different targets (return vs. volatility), trading setups (long top-decile and short bottom-decile vs. trade-all), and metrics (return spread between top and bottom 20% (Q5-Q1) vs. mean squared error (MSE)), making direct comparison and connection challenging. We bridge these communities with EarningsInOne, the first corpus aligning earnings news, ECTs, and intraday and next-day prices across SP 1500 (broad U.S. equity universe, 2022-2025). Applying unified trading and evaluation tools to both signal types, we confirm a clean speed separation, fast numbers, slow language: quantitative surprise peaks at announcement and is largely eliminated by the next market open; qualitative ECT sentiment peaks on the next trading day, real and tradeable, but hidden under prior transcript-based evaluation that optimised sign-agnostic volatility with pointwise MSE.
core_methodology: The paper introduces EarningsInOne, a corpus that aligns earnings news, earnings conference call transcripts (ECTs), and intraday and next-day prices across the SP 1500. It applies unified trading and evaluation tools to both quantitative surprise (numeric earnings-per-share/revenue versus analyst estimates) and qualitative language (management tone, guidance, Q&A credibility) to study their sequential impact on markets.
data_sources: Earnings news, earnings conference call transcripts (ECTs), and intraday and next-day prices across the SP 1500 (broad U.S. equity universe, 2022-2025).
alpha_potential: The paper identifies a clear temporal separation between quantitative and qualitative signals in earnings announcements. Quantitative surprise peaks at announcement and is largely eliminated by the next market open, while qualitative ECT sentiment peaks on the next trading day, offering a real and tradeable signal that was previously hidden under traditional evaluation methods.
title_cn: 快速数字，慢速语言：连接定量与定性盈利信号
summary_cn: 该论文通过EarningsInOne语料库，对齐了盈利新闻、盈利电话会议记录（ECTs）及盘中与次日价格数据，研究了定量（数字盈利/收入与分析师预期对比）和定性（管理层语气、指引、问答可信度）信号在盈利公告中的时序影响。研究发现定量信号在公告时达到峰值并在次日开盘前基本消除，而定性信号在次日交易时达到峰值，提供了可交易的alpha信号。

title: CLQT: A Closed-Loop, Cost-Aware, Strategy-Consistent Benchmark for Diagnostic Evaluation of LLM Portfolio-Management Agents
summary: LLM agents are increasingly cast as autonomous portfolio managers, and benchmarks have moved from financial question-answering to sequential trading. Yet most still rank agents by returns over a fixed window -- a weak proxy, since a period's return is dominated by the market path and apparent alpha can dissolve once look-ahead leakage is controlled. Such a ranking certifies neither sound reasoning, nor a consistent strategy, nor a durable edge. We introduce CLQT, which reframes closed-loop trading evaluation as diagnosis rather than ranking: an instrument that localizes where and why an agent's process succeeds or fails. CLQT is a fully closed-loop, cost-aware, strategy-consistent, temporally-gated environment whose agents run a five-stage cycle: gather, synthesize, allocate, execute, reflect. Each round emits a complete DecisionRound sealed into a recompute-verifiable hash chain, so every metric is reconstructable from the trail. Six pillars form the substrate: a hard TimeGate, institutional transaction- and financing-cost modeling, strategy-consistency scoring, three-tier memory, a Model-Context-Protocol tool layer, and mandate-aware synthesis. The same agent runs as a constrained committee of specialized roles or a single full-autonomy orchestrator, making process scaffolding an experimental variable. From the audit trail we compute a five-axis capability scorecard (APM-CS: Coherence, Acuity, Composure, Discipline, Reliability), with Coherence judged partly by a held-out, out-of-cohort LLM to curb self-preference bias. We validate it on a contamination-controlled multi-model backtest with an ablation grid and a live broker track on unseen, post-cutoff data, against a repeated-run noise floor. CLQT separates outcome from capability, yielding not a model ranking but a durable, extensible map of agent competencies and limitations.
core_methodology: CLQT introduces a closed-loop, cost-aware, strategy-consistent benchmark for evaluating LLM-based portfolio management agents. It focuses on diagnosing agent performance through a five-stage cycle (gather, synthesize, allocate, execute, reflect) and uses a six-pillar framework including time gating, cost modeling, strategy-consistency scoring, and a Model-Context-Protocol tool layer. The methodology emphasizes reconstructable metrics via a hash chain and evaluates agents on a five-axis capability scorecard (APM-CS).
data_sources: The paper does not explicitly mention specific data sources but implies the use of market data for backtesting and live broker tracking. The framework is designed to be adaptable to various financial datasets.
alpha_potential: The framework's focus on strategy consistency, cost awareness, and closed-loop evaluation helps identify durable edges in LLM-based trading agents. By separating outcome from capability, it can uncover true alpha potential beyond mere returns, particularly in avoiding look-ahead leakage and self-preference bias.
title_cn: CLQT：一种闭环、成本感知、策略一致的基准测试方法，用于诊断评估LLM投资组合管理代理
summary_cn: CLQT提出了一种闭环、成本感知且策略一致的基准测试框架，用于评估基于LLM的投资组合管理代理。该框架通过五个阶段（收集、合成、分配、执行、反思）和六个支柱（时间门控、成本建模、策略一致性评分等）诊断代理性能，强调可重构的指标和五维能力评分（APM-CS）。该方法有助于识别真正的alpha潜力，避免前瞻性泄漏和自我偏好偏差，适用于实际交易场景。

title: Liquidity-Based Audit of Algorithmic Trading Strategies
summary: We show that net demand for liquidity by algo strategies is identifiable from its trade and price history alone, with no knowledge of its signal or optimization problem. An exact multi-period regret decomposition implies that the sign of this statistic classifies a linear strategy as a net liquidity consumer or provider, recovering the Kyle (1985) informed-trader/market-maker dichotomy from observables alone. Under an AR(1) cost process, the same statistic equals the product of strategy size and the squared Roll (1984) implied spread, making the correction a direct proxy for prevailing illiquidity. Extending to endogenous price impact and aggregating across N correlated strategies yields a liquidity-balance condition whose violation produces welfare loss scaling as N squared, a closed-form fire-sale externality. We calibrate to CRSP equity data (2016-2025), tracking implied spreads through the COVID-19 and 2022 rate-shock episodes, with an estimator computable in O(Tnd) time.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a method to identify the net demand for liquidity by algorithmic trading strategies using only trade and price history, without knowledge of the strategy's signal or optimization problem. It provides a multi-period regret decomposition to classify strategies as net liquidity consumers or providers and extends this to endogenous price impact and correlated strategies, offering a liquidity-balance condition.
data_sources: CRSP equity data (2016-2025), tracking implied spreads through the COVID-19 and 2022 rate-shock episodes.
alpha_potential: The methodology can be used to identify and classify algorithmic trading strategies based on their liquidity impact, which is crucial for understanding market microstructure and optimizing trading strategies to minimize adverse selection and improve execution quality. The closed-form fire-sale externality provides insights into systemic risks and welfare losses in high-frequency trading environments.
title_cn: 基于流动性的算法交易策略审计
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种仅通过交易和价格历史来识别算法交易策略对流动性的净需求的方法，无需了解策略的信号或优化问题。通过多期遗憾分解，该方法能够将线性策略分类为净流动性消费者或提供者，并扩展到内生价格影响和相关策略，提供了流动性平衡条件。这对于理解市场微观结构、优化交易策略以减少不利选择和改善执行质量具有重要价值。

title: KineticSim: A Lightweight, High-Performance Execution Engine for Real-Time Market Simulators
summary: Simulating financial markets at scale with multi-agent (Agent-Based) models is critical for market design, regulatory stress-testing, and reinforcement learning, but traditional CPU simulators are bottlenecked by sequential processing while vectorized GPU frameworks suffer from kernel-launch overhead and redundant global-memory round-trips. We formalize, analyze, and evaluate a reusable parallel design pattern: persistent, state-carrying clearing for iterative multi-agent reductions. By caching mutable simulation state in thread-block shared memory across step boundaries, aggregating agent actions via shared-memory atomics, and resolving the clearing function cooperatively, the pattern reduces the per-step critical-path depth from Theta(L+A) for sequential clearing (L price-grid ticks, A agents) to Theta(log L + ceil(A/L)) and makes global-memory traffic independent of the step count. We implement this in KineticSim, a lightweight GPU execution engine that simulates massive ensembles of limit-order books in parallel, reaching a peak throughput of over 54.7 billion agent-events per second. On a fixed workload it delivers speedups of 3406x over CPU (NumPy), 27.8x over PyTorch GPU, 42.8x over JAX GPU, and 8.4x over a naive custom CUDA baseline, while using roughly an order of magnitude less GPU memory than PyTorch. Across 53 configurations the two custom CUDA engines produce bitwise-identical order books, and aggregate statistics match the CPU reference to within 0.1%. The pattern generalizes to other iterative multi-agent workloads requiring state-persistent, block-localized reductions.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a lightweight GPU execution engine (KineticSim) that uses a parallel design pattern for high-performance market simulation. It leverages persistent, state-carrying clearing for iterative multi-agent reductions, caching simulation state in thread-block shared memory and aggregating agent actions via shared-memory atomics. This approach significantly reduces critical-path depth and global-memory traffic, enabling massive parallel simulations of limit-order books.
data_sources: The methodology is designed for simulating financial markets, particularly limit-order books, but does not specify real-world data sources. It focuses on synthetic or simulated market data for testing and validation.
alpha_potential: KineticSim's high-performance execution engine can be used to develop and test trading strategies at scale, particularly for high-frequency trading (HFT), market-making, and reinforcement learning-based strategies. Its ability to simulate large ensembles of limit-order books quickly and accurately allows for robust backtesting and stress-testing of strategies under various market conditions.
title_cn: KineticSim：一种轻量级高性能实时市场模拟器执行引擎
summary_cn: KineticSim是一种基于GPU的高性能市场模拟器执行引擎，采用并行设计模式，显著提升了多代理市场模拟的效率。该技术可广泛应用于高频交易策略的开发、市场微观结构研究以及强化学习模型的训练，为量化交易提供高效的仿真环境。

title: The Bounce Has No Direction: Sign, Magnitude, and the Microstructure of Equity Return Predictability
summary: SPY's lag-1 return autocorrelation ($\hat\rho(1)=-0.081$, $z=-7.4$) is among the most significant regularities in empirical equity finance, yet the standard variance-ratio (VR) test cannot determine whether it reflects directional reversal or magnitude shrinkage - phenomena with entirely different trading implications. We develop the Fourier-Residue Identity (FRI), which decomposes return autocorrelation into a sign ($k=2$) and a magnitude ($k=4$) channel, each independently testable and neither redundant. Applied to six US instruments over 1993--2026 and a 21-instrument cross-asset panel, the FRI delivers a sharp microstructure diagnosis. The lag-1 autocorrelation in SPY is driven entirely by magnitude: the FRI sign test is insignificant ($p=0.11$) while the full test achieves $p<10^{-12}$. A large move yesterday predicts a smaller move today regardless of direction - the fingerprint of bid-ask bounce and non-synchronous constituent staleness, not directional reversal. At lag 3, a significant directional reversal ($p=0.02$) invisible to the scalar ACF reveals a separate partial-price-adjustment channel. We prove the Fejer identity VR(q)=1+2C_q (confirmed to <0.001 on all series), giving the Lo-MacKinlay test a spectral interpretation, and introduce a subsample diagnostic R_N=G_{N/2}/G_N that classifies equity autocorrelation as structural (R_N->1) rather than sampling noise (R_N->sqrt(2)). The cross-asset panel shows mean reversion confined to exchange-traded equities and sovereign bonds; credit ETFs, commodities, FX, and crypto are indistinguishable from random walks. All estimators pass 27 unit tests; Monte Carlo confirms correct 5% size under GARCH.
core_methodology: The paper introduces the Fourier-Residue Identity (FRI), a novel method to decompose return autocorrelation into sign and magnitude channels, each independently testable. This approach provides a sharp microstructure diagnosis by distinguishing between directional reversal and magnitude shrinkage effects in return autocorrelations.
data_sources: The study uses data from six US instruments over 1993–2026 and a 21-instrument cross-asset panel, including SPY, exchange-traded equities, sovereign bonds, credit ETFs, commodities, FX, and crypto.
alpha_potential: The FRI method identifies that the lag-1 autocorrelation in SPY is driven by magnitude shrinkage, not directional reversal, indicating bid-ask bounce and non-synchronous constituent staleness. This insight can be leveraged to refine trading strategies by focusing on magnitude-based predictions rather than directional signals. Additionally, the discovery of directional reversal at lag 3 reveals a separate partial-price-adjustment channel, offering further alpha potential.
title_cn: 反弹无方向：符号、幅度与股票收益预测的微观结构
summary_cn: 该论文通过傅里叶残差身份（FRI）方法，将收益自相关分解为符号和幅度通道，发现SPY的滞后1自相关完全由幅度驱动，而非方向反转。这一发现对量化交易策略具有重要应用价值，可优化基于幅度的预测模型。此外，滞后3的方向反转揭示了部分价格调整通道，为策略开发提供了新的信号来源。

title: Entropy Regularized Reinforcement Learning for Zero-Sum Stochastic Differential Games in a Regime-Switching Jump-Diffusion Process
summary: To address parameter misspecification and sudden structural environmental changes in conventional stochastic differential game (SDG) frameworks, this paper introduces a distributional control approach that characterizes optimal strategies as probability distributions over actions, conditioned on the continuous state, the discrete regime state, and parameters. This forms a reinforcement learning framework for entropy-regularized zero-sum stochastic differential games (ERRL-ZSSDGs) in a regime-switching jump-diffusion process. Using the dynamic programming principle (DPP), we derive the associated coupled systems of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman-Isaacs (HJBI) equations, from which equilibrium strategies are expressed via gradients of the value function. For linear-quadratic problems, semi-analytical solutions for both value function and equilibrium strategies are obtained by solving a system of coupled ordinary differential equations (ODEs). In more general settings, an Actor-Critic policy improvement algorithm is developed to approximate the value functions and equilibrium policies across different regimes. The method is applied to an investment game, and numerical examples illustrate the effect of the temperature parameter and regime transitions on optimal policies and values.
core_methodology: Entropy-regularized reinforcement learning for zero-sum stochastic differential games in regime-switching jump-diffusion processes, utilizing dynamic programming principle (DPP) and Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman-Isaacs (HJBI) equations for equilibrium strategies.
data_sources: Theoretical framework applicable to various financial markets, particularly useful for modeling regime shifts and structural changes in market conditions.
alpha_potential: Potential to identify optimal trading strategies in environments with sudden market regime changes, offering robust solutions for parameter misspecification and structural breaks.
title_cn: 基于熵正则化强化学习的体制转换跳跃扩散过程中的零和随机微分博弈
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种熵正则化强化学习框架，用于解决体制转换跳跃扩散过程中的零和随机微分博弈问题。通过动态规划原理和哈密尔顿-雅可比-贝尔曼-伊萨克斯方程，该方法能够有效处理市场参数误设和结构性突变，为量化交易提供稳健的策略优化方案。数值实验展示了温度参数和体制转换对最优策略的影响，具有较高的实际应用价值。

title: Entropy-Regularized Reinforcement Learning for Linear-Quadratic Stackelberg Differential Games in Regime-Switching Diffusion Models
summary: Stackelberg differential games (SDGs) provide a powerful framework for hierarchical decision-making in stochastic and continuous-time environments, yet their solution remains computationally challenging due to the complexity of traditional dynamic programming and Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman-Isaacs (HJBI) methods, especially in high-dimensional systems. This paper proposes an entropy-regularized reinforcement learning (ERRL) approach for linear-quadratic SDGs (LQ-SDGs) within a continuous-time diffusion framework governed by Markovian regime switching. The key innovation lies in deriving exploratory weakly-coupled HJBI equations with entropy regularization, which promotes stochastic policies that actively avoid suboptimal equilibria -- a limitation of classical SDG methods. Neural networks are integrated to approximate regime-dependent value functions and solve high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) efficiently, while a novel sampling technique enhances computational tractability. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework compared to conventional approaches, particularly in escaping suboptimal traps through exploratory policies. The study highlights the critical role of entropy regularization and neural network approximations in achieving robust solutions for hierarchical decision-making problems under abrupt environmental shifts.
core_methodology: Entropy-regularized reinforcement learning (ERRL) for solving linear-quadratic Stackelberg differential games (LQ-SDGs) in continuous-time diffusion models with Markovian regime switching. The approach leverages neural networks to approximate regime-dependent value functions and solve high-dimensional PDEs efficiently.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular market data but focuses on theoretical framework applicable to stochastic and continuous-time environments, which can be adapted to financial markets with regime-switching characteristics.
alpha_potential: The methodology offers potential for developing robust trading strategies that can adapt to abrupt market regime shifts, a common challenge in quantitative finance. The entropy regularization helps avoid suboptimal equilibria, which could lead to more stable performance in dynamic markets.
title_cn: 基于熵正则化强化学习的马尔可夫切换扩散模型中的线性二次Stackelberg微分博弈
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种熵正则化强化学习方法，用于解决具有马尔可夫切换特性的线性二次Stackelberg微分博弈问题。通过结合神经网络和熵正则化技术，该方法能够有效避免次优均衡，适用于动态市场环境中的分层决策问题。在量化交易中，该方法可应用于开发适应市场状态突变的稳健交易策略。

title: Constrained Tabular Diffusion for Finance
summary: Generative models in finance face the dual challenge of producing realistic data while satisfying strict regulatory and economic objectives, a requirement that standard tabular diffusion models cannot provide. To address this difficulty, we introduce Constrained Tabular Diffusion for Finance (CTDF), a novel integration of sampling-time feasibility operations with mixed-type tabular diffusion in financial applications. By incorporating a training-free feasibility operator into the reverse-diffusion sampling loop, CTDF enforces hard constraints for applications such as simulation, legal compliance, and extrapolation. Extensive experiments on large-scale financial datasets demonstrate zero constraint violations and improvement in scarce data utility. CTDF establishes a robust method for generating trustworthy and compliant synthetic data, opening new avenues for rigorous generative modeling and analysis in the financial domain.
core_methodology: Constrained Tabular Diffusion for Finance (CTDF) integrates sampling-time feasibility operations with mixed-type tabular diffusion to generate synthetic financial data that adheres to strict regulatory and economic constraints. The method incorporates a training-free feasibility operator into the reverse-diffusion sampling loop to enforce hard constraints.
data_sources: Large-scale financial datasets (specific types not mentioned in the abstract, but likely includes structured financial data such as transaction records, market data, or regulatory reports).
alpha_potential: CTDF can enhance synthetic data generation for applications like simulation, legal compliance, and extrapolation, which could improve backtesting environments, stress testing, and scenario analysis in quantitative trading. The zero constraint violations and improved data utility in scarce data scenarios suggest potential for more robust and compliant model training.
title_cn: 金融领域的约束表格扩散模型
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种名为CTDF的新方法，通过结合采样时间可行性操作和混合类型表格扩散，生成符合严格监管和经济目标的合成金融数据。该方法在反向扩散采样循环中引入无训练的可行性算子，确保硬约束的满足。实验表明，CTDF在大型金融数据集上实现了零约束违规，并提高了稀缺数据的实用性。这对于量化交易中的模拟测试、合规性检查和极端场景分析具有重要应用价值。

title: FinInvest-GTCN: Explainable Graph-Temporal-Causal Modeling for Risk-Aware Investment Decision Optimization
summary: Venture capital (VC) investment decisions face distinct challenges, such as multi-source heterogeneous data, non-stationary time series, and the demand for explainable predictions in high-stakes, low-data settings. To overcome these issues, we introduce \textbf{FinInvest-GTCN}, a Graph-Temporal-Causal Network that redefines the task from content recommendation to quantitative risk-return assessment. This architecture combines a relational graph encoder to capture the investment ecosystem's topology, a multi-scale temporal fusion module to handle long-term dependencies and non-stationarity, and a causal decision head that generates risk-adjusted predictions with interpretable causal attributions. A core innovation is the Meta-Causal Adaptation (MCA) strategy, which facilitates robust fine-tuning for new, data-scarce sectors by aligning updates with causally-plausible structures derived from meta-pretraining. Comprehensive experiments on proprietary VC datasets show that FinInvest-GTCN delivers state-of-the-art results, markedly lowering the primary Risk-Adjusted Mean Squared Error (RA-MSE) to 2.51 from a baseline of 3.05 and boosting the cumulative return of a simulated portfolio by 18.7\%. Ablation studies underscore the essential role of each component, while additional analyses confirm the model's stability, interpretability, and enhanced adaptability. This work pioneers a data-driven, explainable framework for investment decision support.
core_methodology: Graph-Temporal-Causal Network combining relational graph encoding, multi-scale temporal fusion, and causal decision making with Meta-Causal Adaptation for robust fine-tuning.
data_sources: Proprietary venture capital datasets including multi-source heterogeneous data and non-stationary time series.
alpha_potential: The model captures investment ecosystem topology and long-term dependencies, providing risk-adjusted predictions with interpretable causal attributions, potentially identifying mispriced assets in VC markets.
title_cn: FinInvest-GTCN：基于图-时序-因果建模的可解释风险感知投资决策优化方法
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种创新的图-时序-因果网络模型，通过整合投资生态系统的拓扑结构、多尺度时序特征和因果推理，为风险资本投资提供可解释的量化决策支持。核心创新Meta-Causal Adaptation策略使模型能在数据稀缺的新领域保持稳健表现，实验显示其显著提升了风险调整后收益（18.7%回报提升）。该框架对量化投资中处理复杂关联和非平稳时序数据具有重要参考价值。

title: A3M: Adaptive, Adversarial and Multi-Objective Learning for Strategic Bidding in Repeated Auctions
summary: Learning to bid in repeated multi-unit auctions with bandit feedback poses a fundamental challenge. Existing methods often rely on rigid explore-then-exploit schedules, assume stationary adversaries, and optimize solely for bidder utility, thereby limiting adaptability and strategic robustness. To address these limitations, we introduce the A3M framework, which integrates adaptive deep reinforcement learning (DRL), explicit adversarial reasoning, and principled multi-objective reward design for online auction strategy optimization. A3M employs an actor-critic DRL backbone to dynamically balance exploration and exploitation, an opponent model for fictitious play against non-stationary adversaries, and a composite reward function to jointly maximize utility, auctioneer revenue, and fairness. We provide the first comprehensive empirical evaluation of this integrated approach against established baselines in both discriminatory and uniform price auctions. Results show that A3M reduces final regret by 30--40\% in standard settings, maintains robust performance against adversarial strategy shifts, scales favorably with the number of units $K$, and enables tunable multi-objective trade-offs. An extensive ablation study confirms the necessity of each core component. Our work establishes A3M as a powerful and flexible framework for learning in complex auction environments.
core_methodology: Adaptive deep reinforcement learning (DRL) with actor-critic backbone, explicit adversarial reasoning via opponent modeling, and multi-objective reward design for online auction strategy optimization.
data_sources: Simulated or real-world repeated multi-unit auctions with bandit feedback, potentially applicable to financial auctions like treasury or bond auctions.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to dynamically balance exploration and exploitation, adapt to non-stationary adversaries, and optimize for multiple objectives (utility, revenue, fairness) could be leveraged in financial auctions to gain a competitive edge. The 30-40% reduction in final regret indicates strong performance improvement potential.
title_cn: A3M：用于重复拍卖中策略性竞标的自适应、对抗性和多目标学习框架
summary_cn: A3M框架通过结合自适应深度强化学习、显式对抗推理和多目标奖励设计，为复杂拍卖环境中的策略优化提供了强大工具。在金融拍卖（如国债拍卖）中，该框架可动态平衡探索与利用，适应非静态对手，并优化多目标（效用、收入、公平性），具有30-40%的遗憾减少，展现出在实际交易中的高应用潜力。

title: When Summaries Distort Decisions: Information Fidelity in LLM-Compressed Financial Analysis
summary: Financial decision-makers face more information than they can directly inspect, making context compression necessary. Yet when large language models (LLMs) compress financial source material, they can alter the investment judgment supported by the original source. We frame this problem as information fidelity: compression loses fidelity when it changes the decision induced by the source. In agentic systems, such losses may recur across intermediate steps and amplify throughout the decision process. Across financial filings and earnings-call transcripts, we find that LLM-based compression can produce fluent and factually plausible compressed contexts that nevertheless alter downstream decisions. We analyze two diagnostic patterns associated with fidelity loss: decontextualization, where salient evidence is retained but separated from the caveats and contextual qualifiers needed for correct interpretation, and model dependency, where different compressors expose different views of the same source. We then propose Agentic Context Compression, which generates multiple candidate compressions and audits their disagreements against the original source. Our results suggest that financial compression should be evaluated not only by efficiency or factuality, but also by its ability to preserve decision-relevant context.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Agentic Context Compression, a method that generates multiple candidate compressions of financial documents using LLMs and audits their disagreements against the original source to ensure fidelity in decision-making. It specifically addresses decontextualization and model dependency issues in LLM-based compression.
data_sources: Financial filings and earnings-call transcripts, which are common sources of unstructured financial data used in quantitative analysis.
alpha_potential: By improving the fidelity of compressed financial information, this methodology can enhance the accuracy of AI-driven investment decisions, potentially uncovering more reliable signals from unstructured data that traditional methods might miss or distort.
title_cn: 当摘要扭曲决策时：LLM压缩金融分析中的信息保真度
summary_cn: 本研究针对金融决策者在处理大量信息时面临的挑战，提出了一种基于LLM的上下文压缩方法，通过生成多个候选压缩版本并审核其与原始源的分歧，确保决策相关上下文的保真度。对于量化交易而言，该方法可提高从财务文件和财报电话会议转录中提取信号的准确性，减少信息压缩过程中的失真，从而增强AI驱动投资决策的可靠性。

title: A Mathematical Optimization Approach for Expert-Informed Bayesian Best Subset Selection
summary: A central challenge in statistical modeling is identifying the subset of features that belong in the true regression model. The classical best subset selection problem, recently made tractable via mixed-integer optimization (MIO), finds the globally optimal sparse solution. It does not, however, make use of any information beyond the observed data. In many applied settings, domain experts can meaningfully rank or score the relevance of candidate predictors, yet no existing framework integrates such probabilistic expert assessments directly into the best-subsets objective. This paper presents Expert-Implied Bayesian Best Subsets (EBBS), a method that incorporates domain-expert probability estimates of feature relevance into the MIO best-subsets problem through a maximum a posteriori (MAP) framework. Expert views from multiple respondents are aggregated into a single prior probability per feature using the Poisson binomial distribution for marginal probability estimates, the pairwise win rate for pairwise comparisons, or the normalized mean rank for ordinal rankings. This probability enters the objective function as a log-odds penalty term that smoothly encourages or discourages the selection of each feature consistent with the expert consensus. This paper provides analytic derivations of the MAP formulation and characterizes its theoretical properties. The proposed model reduces to Best Subsets when experts all have no views. Empirical results on synthetic and real datasets are forthcoming.
core_methodology: Expert-Implied Bayesian Best Subsets (EBBS) integrates domain-expert probability estimates into the mixed-integer optimization (MIO) best-subsets problem through a maximum a posteriori (MAP) framework. This method aggregates expert views into a single prior probability per feature, which is then used to encourage or discourage the selection of features in the model.
data_sources: The paper mentions empirical results on synthetic and real datasets, though specific financial datasets are not detailed in the abstract.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be applied to feature selection in quantitative trading models, particularly in scenarios where domain expertise can inform the relevance of predictors. This could enhance model robustness and interpretability, potentially leading to better-performing trading strategies.
title_cn: 专家启发的贝叶斯最佳子集选择的数学优化方法
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种专家启发的贝叶斯最佳子集选择方法（EBBS），通过最大后验概率（MAP）框架将领域专家的概率估计整合到混合整数优化（MIO）最佳子集问题中。该方法在量化交易中可用于特征选择，特别是在专家知识可以指导预测变量相关性的场景中，有望提升模型的稳健性和解释性，从而优化交易策略表现。

title: The CRISTAL Method: Neurosymbolic analysis from AI-synthesized world models
summary: This project introduces the CRISTAL Method (Coherent Reliable Intentional Synthesis of Truthful Analysis Logic), a neurosymbolic framework for automating complex analysis workflows, with fundamental investment analysis as a primary use case. This domain poses major challenges: high structural uncertainty, noisy and subjective data, tight attention budgets, and the need for justified, reproducible decisions. Human analysts often struggle in this domain due to cognitive biases and limitations, suggesting significant value in automation. But while LLM-based agents have been proposed as analytical aids, their limitations -- poor numerical reasoning, unawareness of uncertainty, and lack of reproducibility -- hinder their effectiveness in this context. CRISTAL addresses these gaps through a principled blend of statistical model synthesis, continuous learning, and active learning. Starting from a natural-language prior knowledge curriculum, CRISTAL builds a dynamic, interpretable probabilistic program that enables full Bayesian inference, including uncertainty quantification and budget-aware data acquisition. CRISTAL continually refines its world model during analysis, leveraging LLMs for code synthesis and learning. We validate CRISTAL on a novel benchmark of synthetic equities with rich financial and textual data. On a company classification task, CRISTAL achieves Bayes-optimal accuracy with just 5 examples and a 5-second budget, outperforming state-of-the-art LLMs that plateau around 40\% accuracy even with order-of-magnitude more input data and compute.
core_methodology: The CRISTAL Method combines neurosymbolic analysis with probabilistic programming and active learning to automate complex investment analysis workflows. It leverages LLMs for code synthesis and learning, while building dynamic, interpretable probabilistic programs for full Bayesian inference, including uncertainty quantification and budget-aware data acquisition.
data_sources: Synthetic equities with rich financial and textual data, validated on a novel benchmark.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to achieve Bayes-optimal accuracy with minimal data and compute, outperforming state-of-the-art LLMs, suggests potential for generating high-quality, interpretable signals in financial markets. Its focus on uncertainty quantification and reproducible decisions could be valuable for risk-aware trading strategies.
title_cn: CRISTAL方法：基于AI合成世界模型的神经符号分析
summary_cn: CRISTAL方法通过神经符号框架结合概率编程和主动学习，自动化复杂投资分析流程。其在合成股票数据上验证的高效性和准确性，以及不确定性量化和可解释性，为量化交易提供了新的信号生成和风险管理工具。

title: Heads, Not Backbones: Output Heads Dominate Architectures on Fat-Tailed Returns
summary: In a deep forecasting pipeline for fat-tailed financial returns at short horizons, which matters more - the backbone architecture or the output head? We compare four modern backbones (TimesNet, DLinear, N-BEATS, iTransformer) under three output heads: a point head, a single-Gaussian density head, and a Gaussian mixture density head with K=4 components. On S and P 500 monthly log-returns (1871-2023) under anchored walk-forward validation, the three heads form a strict gradient: switching from point to Gaussian improves CRPS by about 1.3 percent; switching from Gaussian to mixture adds a further about 2.4 percent. Switching between backbones, in contrast, changes CRPS by less than 1.5 percent on the point-head row and on the backbone-mean axis; density-head backbone spread is larger (up to 5.1 percent on the h=1 Gaussian row, driven by N-BEATS) but the head gradient (3.7 percentage points) still dominates. The Model Confidence Set on squared errors does not exclude any of the 12 variants at the 5 percent level: the head separates them only on distributional metrics (CRPS, pinball, coverage), not on squared error. The mixture head incremental value over a single Gaussian is largest in the highest-volatility regimes (13.9 percent in 1970s stagflation at h=12), confirming the mixture captures tail risk beyond what a unimodal Gaussian can express. The picture is horizon-dependent: the head dominates at short horizons, but at long horizons (h >= 6) the backbone re-takes the lead - an h-split we document against classical baselines (section 5.1). We conclude that on fat-tailed returns at short horizons, the head dominates the backbone, and the mixture distribution adds genuine value over a single Gaussian during crisis periods when risk-management decisions actually matter.
core_methodology: The paper compares the effectiveness of different output heads (point, single-Gaussian, Gaussian mixture) versus backbone architectures (TimesNet, DLinear, N-BEATS, iTransformer) in forecasting fat-tailed financial returns. The study uses anchored walk-forward validation to evaluate performance metrics like CRPS, pinball, and coverage.
data_sources: S&P 500 monthly log-returns from 1871 to 2023.
alpha_potential: The study demonstrates that output heads, particularly Gaussian mixture density heads, significantly improve forecasting accuracy for fat-tailed returns, especially during high-volatility regimes. This suggests potential for better risk management and tail risk prediction in trading strategies.
title_cn: 头部而非骨干：在厚尾收益中输出头部主导架构
summary_cn: 该研究比较了不同输出头部（点预测、单高斯密度、高斯混合密度）与骨干架构在预测厚尾金融收益中的效果。结果表明，在高波动时期，高斯混合密度头部显著提升预测精度，尤其在风险管理决策关键时期。

title: Adaptive Iterative Hard Thresholding for Online High-dimensional Quantile Regression
summary: Online high-dimensional regression requires algorithms that can update sequentially while preserving structural sparsity. We propose \textit{Adaptive Iterative Hard Thresholding (AIHT)}, an online sparse-regression framework that alternates stochastic subgradient updates with adaptively scheduled hard-thresholding steps. The key idea is to separate support discovery from local refinement: early in the learning process, AIHT delays thresholding so that weak but informative coordinates have time to accumulate signal, while later it increases the projection frequency to stabilize the sparse estimator and exploit local curvature. We develop the theory for high-dimensional online quantile regression, a challenging setting in which the loss is nonsmooth and the data may exhibit heterogeneity or heavy-tailed noise. Under restricted curvature and gradient-leakage conditions, AIHT remains in an inflated sparse cone, exhibits a two-phase convergence behavior, and attains logarithmic regret for the sliding-window objective. Simulations for online quantile regression, together with threshold-scheduling ablations, support the proposed mechanism and illustrate its advantage over standard online sparse-learning baselines.
core_methodology: Adaptive Iterative Hard Thresholding (AIHT) is an online sparse-regression framework that alternates stochastic subgradient updates with adaptively scheduled hard-thresholding steps. It separates support discovery from local refinement, delaying thresholding early to accumulate signal and increasing projection frequency later to stabilize the sparse estimator.
data_sources: The paper focuses on high-dimensional online quantile regression, which can be applied to various financial data sources such as stock prices, trading volumes, or other market microstructure data.
alpha_potential: The methodology can be used to identify sparse but informative signals in high-dimensional financial data, potentially uncovering hidden patterns or inefficiencies in market behavior, especially in scenarios with heavy-tailed noise or heterogeneous data.
title_cn: 在线高维分位数回归的自适应迭代硬阈值方法
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种自适应迭代硬阈值（AIHT）方法，用于在线高维分位数回归。该方法通过交替进行随机次梯度更新和自适应硬阈值步骤，有效处理高维稀疏数据。在金融交易中，该方法可用于识别市场中的稀疏信号，尤其是在噪声较大或数据异质的情况下，具有潜在的应用价值。

title: MACROCAST: A Vintage-Consistent Time Series Foundation Model for Real-Time Macroeconomic Forecasting
summary: We introduce MACROCAST, a lightweight Time Series Foundation Model (TSFM) for real-time macroeconomic forecasting. Existing TSFMs suffer from data leakage in two forms: temporal contamination, as the model may have seen the realized values of the series it forecasts, and revision bias, as training on fully revised data diverges from the preliminary, vintage-specific releases available to real-time forecasters. MACROCAST is, to our knowledge, the first TSFM that rules out both forms of leakage entirely: at no stage of training is the model exposed to information that would not have been available to a forecaster in real time. We train MACROCAST first on purely synthetic time series in approximately one GPU-day and then fine-tune it on synthetic time series drawn from Bayesian VARs, dynamic factor models, and ARIMA specifications estimated on vintage-specific ALFRED data. Because pretraining uses only simulated data and fine-tuning uses only real-time vintages, no observed future or revised value ever enters the model; each fine-tuning run takes nine minutes. Evaluated on the FRED-MD database in a genuine real-time out-of-sample exercise, MACROCAST improves on the AR(1) benchmark for roughly 80% of series-horizon pairs, matches or surpasses Chronos-2 -- the strongest currently available TSFM -- and outperforms the Bayesian VAR and dynamic factor model benchmarks, all in a data-leakage-free manner.
core_methodology: MACROCAST is a Time Series Foundation Model (TSFM) designed for real-time macroeconomic forecasting, trained first on synthetic time series and then fine-tuned on vintage-specific ALFRED data. It avoids data leakage by ensuring no future or revised data is used during training.
data_sources: Synthetic time series, vintage-specific ALFRED data, and FRED-MD database for evaluation.
alpha_potential: The model's ability to provide accurate real-time macroeconomic forecasts without data leakage can be valuable for macroeconomic-driven trading strategies, such as those based on interest rate changes or GDP growth predictions.
title_cn: MACROCAST：一种用于实时宏观经济预测的版本一致时间序列基础模型
summary_cn: MACROCAST是一种轻量级时间序列基础模型，专为实时宏观经济预测设计。它通过避免数据泄漏（包括时间污染和修订偏差），在真实时间外样本测试中表现优于现有基准模型。该模型在合成数据上预训练，并在特定版本的ALFRED数据上微调，为宏观经济驱动的交易策略提供了可靠的预测工具。

title: ProSpec RL: Plan Ahead, then Execute
summary: Imagining potential outcomes of actions before execution helps agents make more informed decisions, a prospective thinking ability fundamental to human cognition. However, mainstream model-free Reinforcement Learning (RL) methods lack the ability to proactively envision future scenarios, plan, and guide strategies. These methods typically rely on trial and error to adjust policy functions, aiming to maximize cumulative rewards or long-term value, even if such high-reward decisions place the environment in extremely dangerous states. To address this, we propose the Prospective (ProSpec) RL method, which makes higher-value, lower-risk optimal decisions by imagining future n-stream trajectories. Specifically, ProSpec employs a dynamic model to predict future states (termed "imagined states") based on the current state and a series of sampled actions. Furthermore, we integrate the concept of Model Predictive Control and introduce a cycle consistency constraint that allows the agent to evaluate and select the optimal actions from these trajectories. Moreover, ProSpec employs cycle consistency to mitigate two fundamental issues in RL: augmenting state reversibility to avoid irreversible events (low risk) and augmenting actions to generate numerous virtual trajectories, thereby improving data efficiency. We validated the effectiveness of our method on the DMControl benchmarks, where our approach achieved significant performance improvements. Code will be open-sourced upon acceptance.
core_methodology: Prospective (ProSpec) RL method that employs a dynamic model to predict future states (imagined states) based on the current state and sampled actions. It integrates Model Predictive Control and cycle consistency constraints to evaluate and select optimal actions from these trajectories, aiming for higher-value, lower-risk decisions.
data_sources: The paper validates the method on DMControl benchmarks, which are typically used in robotics and control tasks. However, the methodology can be adapted to financial time series data for trading applications.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to envision future scenarios and plan ahead could be leveraged in trading to anticipate market movements and adjust strategies proactively, potentially capturing alpha by avoiding high-risk states and optimizing long-term value.
title_cn: ProSpec RL：先规划后执行
summary_cn: ProSpec RL方法通过动态模型预测未来状态，结合模型预测控制和循环一致性约束，选择最优行动轨迹。该方法在金融交易中可应用于前瞻性市场预测和风险管理，通过避免高风险状态和优化长期价值来提升交易策略表现。

title: fev-bench: A Realistic Benchmark for Time Series Forecasting
summary: Benchmark quality is critical for meaningful evaluation and sustained progress in time series forecasting, particularly with the rise of pretrained models. Existing benchmarks often have limited domain coverage or overlook real-world settings such as tasks with covariates. Their aggregation procedures frequently lack statistical rigor, making it unclear whether observed performance differences reflect true improvements or random variation. Many benchmarks lack consistent evaluation infrastructure or are too rigid for integration into existing pipelines. To address these gaps, we propose fev-bench, a benchmark of 100 forecasting tasks across seven domains, including 46 with covariates. Supporting the benchmark, we introduce fev, a lightweight Python library for forecasting evaluation emphasizing reproducibility and integration with existing workflows. Using fev, fev-bench employs principled aggregation with bootstrapped confidence intervals to report performance along two dimensions: win rates and skill scores. We report results on fev-bench for pretrained, statistical, and baseline models and identify promising future research directions.
core_methodology: The paper introduces fev-bench, a benchmark for time series forecasting that includes 100 tasks across seven domains, with 46 tasks involving covariates. It uses a lightweight Python library (fev) for evaluation, emphasizing reproducibility and integration with existing workflows. The benchmark employs principled aggregation with bootstrapped confidence intervals to report performance via win rates and skill scores.
data_sources: The benchmark covers seven domains, though specific financial datasets are not detailed. The inclusion of covariates suggests potential use of alternative data alongside traditional time series data.
alpha_potential: The benchmark's rigorous evaluation framework and inclusion of covariates could help identify robust forecasting models for financial time series, potentially uncovering alpha in areas like momentum strategies or factor investing where accurate forecasts are critical.
title_cn: fev-bench：时间序列预测的现实基准
summary_cn: 该论文提出了fev-bench，一个包含100个任务的跨七领域时间序列预测基准，其中46个任务涉及协变量。通过轻量级Python库fev，该基准强调可重复性和与现有工作流的集成，使用引导置信区间进行严谨的聚合评估。对于量化交易，该基准有助于开发稳健的预测模型，特别是在动量策略和因子投资中。

title: When, How Long and How Much? Interpretable Neural Networks for Time Series Regression by Learning to Mask and Aggregate
summary: Time series extrinsic regression (TSER) refers to the task of predicting a continuous target variable from an input time series. It appears in many domains, including healthcare, finance, environmental monitoring, and engineering. In these settings, accurate predictions and trustworthy reasoning are both essential. Although state-of-the-art TSER models achieve strong predictive performance, they typically operate as black boxes, making it difficult to understand which temporal patterns drive their decisions. Post-hoc interpretability techniques, such as feature attribution, aim to to explain how the model arrives at its predictions, but often produce coarse, noisy, or unstable explanations. Recently, inherently interpretable approaches based on concepts, additive decompositions, or symbolic regression, have emerged as promising alternatives. However, these approaches remain limited: they require explicit supervision on the concepts themselves, often cannot capture interactions between time-series features, lack expressiveness for complex temporal patterns, and struggle to scale to high-dimensional multivariate data. To address these limitations, we propose MAGNETS (Mask-and-AGgregate NEtwork for Time Series), an inherently interpretable neural architecture for TSER. MAGNETS learns a compact set of human-understandable concepts without requiring any annotations. Each concept corresponds to a learned, mask-based aggregation over selected input features, explicitly revealing both which features drive predictions and when they matter in the sequence. Predictions are formed as combinations of these learned concepts through a transparent, additive structure, enabling clear insight into the model's decision process. The code implementation and datasets are publicly available at https://github.com/FlorentF9/MAGNETS.
core_methodology: MAGNETS (Mask-and-AGgregate NEtwork for Time Series) is an inherently interpretable neural architecture that learns a compact set of human-understandable concepts without requiring annotations. Each concept corresponds to a learned, mask-based aggregation over selected input features, revealing which features drive predictions and when they matter in the sequence. Predictions are formed as combinations of these learned concepts through a transparent, additive structure.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular financial datasets, but the methodology is applicable to multivariate time series data commonly used in quantitative finance, such as price series, volume, and other market indicators.
alpha_potential: The interpretability of MAGNETS could help identify and exploit temporal patterns in financial time series that are not easily captured by traditional black-box models. The ability to understand which features and time periods drive predictions can lead to more robust and explainable trading signals, potentially uncovering new alpha sources.
title_cn: 何时、多久和多少？通过学习掩码和聚合实现时间序列回归的可解释神经网络
summary_cn: 该论文提出的MAGNETS方法通过可解释的神经网络架构，学习时间序列中的关键特征和时间段，形成透明化的预测模型。在量化交易中，这种方法可用于识别驱动市场变动的时序模式，提升信号解释性和策略稳健性，尤其适用于需要高透明度的监管环境或复杂多变量分析场景。

title: Weighted Contrastive Learning for Anomaly-Aware Time-Series Forecasting
summary: Reliable forecasting of multivariate time series under anomalous conditions is crucial in applications such as ATM cash logistics, where sudden demand shifts can disrupt operations. Modern deep forecasters achieve high accuracy on normal data but often fail when distribution shifts occur. We propose Weighted Contrastive Adaptation (WECA), a Weighted contrastive objective that aligns normal and anomaly-augmented representations, preserving anomaly-relevant information while maintaining consistency under benign variations. Evaluations on a nationwide ATM transaction dataset with domain-informed anomaly injection show that WECA improves SMAPE on anomaly-affected data by 6.1 percentage points compared to a normally trained baseline, with negligible degradation on normal data. These results demonstrate that WECA enhances forecasting reliability under anomalies without sacrificing performance during regular operations.
core_methodology: Weighted Contrastive Adaptation (WECA) is used to align normal and anomaly-augmented time-series representations, enhancing forecasting reliability under anomalous conditions.
data_sources: Evaluated on a nationwide ATM transaction dataset with domain-informed anomaly injection.
alpha_potential: The method can be adapted to detect and respond to anomalous market conditions, potentially improving trading strategies during market shocks or sudden volatility shifts.
title_cn: 加权对比学习在异常感知时间序列预测中的应用
summary_cn: 该论文提出的加权对比适应方法（WECA）通过对齐正常和异常增强的时间序列表示，提高了在异常条件下的预测可靠性。在量化交易中，该方法可应用于市场异常检测，帮助策略在波动剧烈或突发事件中保持稳健性，具有潜在的市场中性收益机会。

title: CaveAgent: Transforming LLMs into Stateful Runtime Operators
summary: LLM-based agents are increasingly capable of complex task execution, yet current agentic systems remain constrained by text-centric paradigms that struggle with long-horizon tasks due to fragile multi-turn dependencies and context drift. We present CaveAgent, a framework that shifts tool use from ``LLM-as-Text-Generator'' to ``LLM-as-Runtime-Operator.'' CaveAgent introduces a dual-stream architecture that inverts the conventional paradigm: rather than treating the LLM's text context as the primary workspace with tools as auxiliary, CaveAgent elevates the persistent Python runtime as the central locus of state, with a lightweight semantic stream serving as its orchestrator. Beyond leveraging code generation to resolve interdependent sub-tasks (e.g., loops, conditionals) in a single step, CaveAgent introduces \textit{Stateful Runtime Management}: it injects, manipulates, and retrieves complex Python objects (e.g., DataFrames, database connections) that persist across turns, unlike existing code-based approaches that remain text-bound. CaveAgent further provides a runtime-integrated skill management system that extends the Agent Skills open standard, enabling ecosystem interoperability through executable skill injections. This persistence mechanism serves as a high-fidelity external memory that reduces context drift in multi-turn interactions and preserves processed data for downstream applications without information loss. Evaluations show consistent improvement across challenging benchmarks, enabling CaveAgent to handle data scales that cause context overflow in both JSON-based and code-based agents. The accessible runtime state further provides programmatically verifiable feedback, enabling automated evaluation and reward signal generation without human annotation and establishing a structural foundation for future research in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR).
core_methodology: CaveAgent introduces a dual-stream architecture that elevates a persistent Python runtime as the central locus of state, with a lightweight semantic stream serving as its orchestrator. It leverages code generation to resolve interdependent sub-tasks in a single step and introduces Stateful Runtime Management for manipulating complex Python objects that persist across turns.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular data sources but implies the framework can handle various data types including DataFrames and database connections, suggesting flexibility with financial datasets.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to maintain persistent state and handle complex, interdependent tasks could enhance quantitative trading strategies by reducing context drift and improving multi-turn task execution, potentially uncovering alpha through more robust and scalable algorithmic trading systems.
title_cn: CaveAgent：将大语言模型转化为有状态运行时操作符
summary_cn: CaveAgent框架通过双流架构将Python运行时提升为状态中心，轻量级语义流作为协调器，支持复杂Python对象的持久化操作。该技术可减少多轮交互中的上下文漂移，提升量化交易策略的鲁棒性和扩展性，适用于高频交易和复杂投资组合管理。

title: Diff-MN: Diffusion Parameterized MoE-NCDE for Continuous Time Series Generation with Irregular Observations
summary: Time series generation (TSG) is widely used across domains, yet most existing methods assume regular sampling and fixed output resolutions. These assumptions are often violated in practice, where observations are irregular and sparse, while downstream applications require continuous and high-resolution TS. Although Neural Controlled Differential Equation (NCDE) is promising for modeling irregular TS, it is constrained by a single dynamics function, tightly coupled optimization, and limited ability to adapt learned dynamics to newly generated samples from the generative model. We propose Diff-MN, a continuous TSG framework that enhances NCDE with a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) dynamics function and a decoupled architectural design for dynamics-focused training. To further enable NCDE to generalize to newly generated samples, Diff-MN employs a diffusion model to parameterize the NCDE temporal dynamics parameters (MoE weights), i.e., jointly learn the distribution of TS data and MoE weights. This design allows sample-specific NCDE parameters to be generated for continuous TS generation. Experiments on ten public and synthetic datasets demonstrate that Diff-MN consistently outperforms strong baselines on both irregular-to-regular and irregular-to-continuous TSG tasks. The code is available at the link https://github.com/microsoft/TimeCraft/tree/main/Diff-MN.
core_methodology: Diff-MN combines Neural Controlled Differential Equations (NCDE) with a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) dynamics function and a diffusion model to parameterize the NCDE temporal dynamics parameters. This allows for continuous time series generation with irregular observations, enhancing the model's ability to adapt to newly generated samples.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the framework on ten public and synthetic datasets, which likely include irregularly sampled time series data. While specific financial datasets are not mentioned, the methodology is applicable to financial time series data with irregular observations.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to generate continuous and high-resolution time series from irregular observations can be valuable for quantitative trading, particularly in scenarios where market data is sparse or irregularly sampled (e.g., low-liquidity assets, alternative data sources). This could help in developing more robust models for price prediction, volatility estimation, or anomaly detection.
title_cn: Diff-MN：基于扩散参数化的MoE-NCDE用于不规则观测的连续时间序列生成
summary_cn: Diff-MN通过结合神经控制微分方程（NCDE）和专家混合（MoE）动态函数，利用扩散模型参数化NCDE的时间动态参数，实现了对不规则观测的连续时间序列生成。这一方法在量化交易中具有潜在应用价值，特别是在处理稀疏或不规则市场数据时，可提升价格预测和波动率估计的模型鲁棒性。

title: Constrained Policy Optimization with Cantelli-Bounded Value-at-Risk
summary: We introduce Canary, a risk-averse method designed to optimize Value-at-Risk (VaR) constrained reinforcement learning (RL) problems. We employ Cantelli's inequality to obtain a tractable, conservative and smooth bound on the VaR constraint based on the first two moments of the cost return. This yields a constraint estimator that remains stable with tight violation thresholds in dense cost regimes. Extending the trust-region framework of the Constrained Policy Optimization (CPO) method, we further provide worst-case bounds for both policy improvement and constraint violation during the training process. Empirically, across continuous-control safety benchmarks, Canary most reliably satisfies its constraint, with the fewest violations and the earliest permanent satisfaction, while remaining reward-competitive with other baselines that also satisfy.
core_methodology: Canary employs Cantelli's inequality to create a tractable, conservative bound on Value-at-Risk (VaR) in reinforcement learning (RL) problems. It extends the Constrained Policy Optimization (CPO) framework with worst-case bounds for policy improvement and constraint violation, ensuring stable and reliable performance in dense cost regimes.
data_sources: The abstract mentions continuous-control safety benchmarks, which typically involve simulated environments. However, the methodology could be adapted to financial time series data for risk-averse trading strategies.
alpha_potential: The method's focus on VaR optimization and risk aversion is highly relevant for portfolio management and algorithmic trading, where controlling downside risk is crucial. The stable constraint satisfaction could lead to more reliable trading strategies under market stress.
title_cn: 基于Cantelli界定的风险价值约束策略优化
summary_cn: Canary方法通过Cantelli不等式为风险价值(VaR)约束提供稳定可靠的界限，适用于风险厌恶型强化学习。在金融交易中，该方法可优化投资组合的VaR控制，尤其在市场波动剧烈时保持策略稳健性，适合风险敏感的量化交易应用。

title: Neural Galerkin Normalizing Flow for Transition Probability Density Functions of Diffusion Models
summary: We propose a new Neural Galerkin Normalizing Flow framework to approximate the transition probability density function of a diffusion process by solving the corresponding Fokker-Planck equation with an atomic initial distribution, parametrically with respect to the location of the initial mass. By using Normalizing Flows, we look for the solution as a transformation of the transition probability density function of a reference stochastic process, ensuring that our approximation is structure-preserving and automatically satisfies positivity and mass conservation constraints. By extending Neural Galerkin schemes to the context of Normalizing Flows, we derive a system of ODEs for the time evolution of the Normalizing Flow's parameters. Adaptive sampling routines are used to evaluate the Fokker-Planck residual in meaningful locations, which is of vital importance to address high-dimensional PDEs. Numerical results show that this strategy captures key features of the true solution and enforces the causal relationship between the initial datum and the density function at subsequent times. After completing an offline training phase, online evaluation becomes significantly more cost-effective than solving the PDE from scratch. The proposed method serves as a promising surrogate model, which could be deployed in many-query problems associated with stochastic differential equations, like Bayesian inference, simulation, and diffusion bridge generation.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a Neural Galerkin Normalizing Flow framework to approximate the transition probability density function of a diffusion process by solving the Fokker-Planck equation. It uses Normalizing Flows to transform the probability density function of a reference stochastic process, ensuring structure-preserving properties and constraints like positivity and mass conservation. The method involves adaptive sampling to evaluate residuals and derives a system of ODEs for parameter evolution.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular market data but focuses on stochastic differential equations (SDEs) and diffusion processes, which are fundamental in modeling financial markets, such as asset price movements and interest rate dynamics.
alpha_potential: This method can be applied to model the transition probabilities of financial assets, which is crucial for pricing derivatives, risk management, and statistical arbitrage. The ability to efficiently approximate these densities offline and deploy them online could provide a competitive edge in high-frequency trading and Bayesian inference for financial models.
title_cn: 扩散模型转移概率密度函数的神经伽辽金归一化流方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种神经伽辽金归一化流框架，用于近似扩散过程的转移概率密度函数。该方法通过求解Fokker-Planck方程，利用归一化流确保解的结构保持和约束条件。在金融交易中，该方法可用于高效建模资产价格动态，适用于衍生品定价、风险管理和统计套利，具有显著的离线训练和在线部署优势。

title: Sustainable Hybrid Document-Routed Retrieval for Financial RAG: Resolving the Robustness-Precision Trade-off
summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems for financial document QA typically follow a chunk-based paradigm: documents are split into fragments, embedded, and retrieved by similarity. In structurally homogeneous corpora such as regulatory filings, this suffers from cross-document chunk confusion. Semantic File Routing (SFR), which uses LLM structured output to route queries to whole documents, reduces catastrophic failures but sacrifices targeted-chunk precision. We identify this robustness-precision trade-off on the FinDER benchmark (1,500 queries across five groups): SFR achieves higher average scores (6.45 vs. 6.02) and fewer failures (10.3% vs. 22.5%), while chunk-based retrieval (CBR) yields more perfect answers (13.8% vs. 8.5%). To resolve it, we propose Hybrid Document-Routed Retrieval (HDRR), a two-stage architecture that uses SFR as a document filter followed by chunk retrieval scoped to the identified document(s), eliminating cross-document confusion while preserving chunk precision. HDRR achieves the best performance on every metric: an average score of 7.54 (25.2% above CBR, 16.9% above SFR), a 6.4% failure rate, 67.7% correctness (+18.7 pp over CBR), and a 20.1% perfect-answer rate (+6.3 pp over CBR, +11.6 pp over SFR), simultaneously attaining the lowest failure rate and highest precision across all five groups. Beyond accuracy, HDRR is also the most efficient of the high-quality systems: it preserves CBR's compact per-query token budget (~5K-15K, an order of magnitude below SFR's ~50K-200K), incurs no indexing-time LLM spend (versus the one-time ~$100 cost of contextual indexing), and uses fewer per-query LLM calls than self-correcting agentic baselines, translating directly to lower API spend and inference-time energy at deployment scale.
core_methodology: Hybrid Document-Routed Retrieval (HDRR) combines Semantic File Routing (SFR) with chunk-based retrieval to improve precision and robustness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems for financial document QA. The two-stage architecture first uses SFR to filter documents and then applies chunk retrieval within the identified documents to eliminate cross-document confusion.
data_sources: Financial documents, specifically regulatory filings, as evidenced by the FinDER benchmark which includes 1,500 queries across five groups.
alpha_potential: The methodology enhances the accuracy and efficiency of retrieving relevant financial information, which can be critical for quantitative trading strategies that rely on precise and timely document analysis. By reducing retrieval failures and improving precision, it can help in identifying key insights from financial documents more reliably.
title_cn: 金融RAG的可持续混合文档路由检索：解决稳健性与精确性的权衡
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种混合文档路由检索（HDRR）方法，通过结合语义文件路由（SFR）和基于分块的检索，显著提高了金融文档问答系统的精确性和稳健性。该方法在FinDER基准测试中表现优异，平均得分提高25.2%，失败率降低至6.4%，完美答案率提升11.6个百分点。这一技术可有效支持量化交易中关键金融信息的快速准确提取。

title: UniMamba: A Unified Spatial-Temporal Modeling Framework with State-Space and Attention Integration
summary: Multivariate time series forecasting is fundamental to numerous domains such as energy, finance, and environmental monitoring, where complex temporal dependencies and cross-variable interactions pose enduring challenges. Existing Transformer-based methods capture temporal correlations through attention mechanisms but suffer from quadratic computational cost, while state-space models like Mamba achieve efficient long-context modeling yet lack explicit temporal pattern recognition. Therefore we introduce UniMamba, a unified spatial-temporal forecasting framework that integrates efficient state-space dynamics with attention-based dependency learning. UniMamba employs a Mamba Variate-Channel Encoding Layer enhanced with FFT-Laplace Transform and TCN to capture global temporal dependencies, and a Spatial Temporal Attention Layer to jointly model inter-variate correlations and temporal evolution. A Feedforward Temporal Dynamics Layer further fuses continuous and discrete contexts for accurate forecasting. Comprehensive experiments on eight public benchmark datasets demonstrate that UniMamba consistently outperforms state-of-the-art forecasting models in both forecasting accuracy and computational efficiency, establishing a scalable and robust solution for long-sequence multivariate time-series prediction.
core_methodology: UniMamba integrates state-space models (Mamba) with attention mechanisms for multivariate time series forecasting. It uses a Mamba Variate-Channel Encoding Layer with FFT-Laplace Transform and TCN to capture global temporal dependencies, and a Spatial Temporal Attention Layer to model inter-variate correlations and temporal evolution. A Feedforward Temporal Dynamics Layer fuses continuous and discrete contexts for forecasting.
data_sources: The paper evaluates UniMamba on eight public benchmark datasets, which likely include financial time series data given the mention of finance in the abstract.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to efficiently model long-context temporal dependencies and cross-variable interactions could be valuable for momentum strategies, factor investing, and arbitrage by identifying complex patterns in financial time series that are not easily captured by traditional models.
title_cn: UniMamba: 具有状态空间与注意力整合的统一时空建模框架
summary_cn: UniMamba是一个高效的时空建模框架，结合了状态空间模型和注意力机制，适用于多变量时间序列预测。其高效的长时间建模和跨变量交互能力可提升金融市场的动量策略和因子投资效果，适用于金融时间序列预测。

title: ITNet: A Learnable Integral Transform That Subsumes Convolution, Attention, and Recurrence
summary: Convolutional networks, recurrent networks, and transformers each encode different inductive biases -- locality, sequential memory, and content-dependent pairwise interaction -- and have remained mathematically distinct since their inception. We show that this fragmentation reflects not a fundamental diversity in how signals should be processed, but rather incomplete views of a single underlying mathematical object: a learnable integral transform. We introduce the Integral Transform Network (ITNet), a unified architecture built around a learnable kernel that depends jointly on positions and features. This kernel is implemented as a small neural network, specifically an MLP, that models pairwise interactions, enabling the model to adapt its behavior from data. We show that convolution, self-attention (including multi-head), and autoregressive recurrence (including LSTM, GRU, S4, and Mamba) arise as special cases under appropriate parameterizations, and that ITNet is a universal approximator of continuous operators. To make this practical, we develop tiled kernel fusion, importance-weighted Monte Carlo integration, and learned low-rank factorization, enabling efficient and scalable computation. A single ITNet architecture with a shared operator and lightweight modality-specific encoders matches or exceeds specialized baselines on ImageNet-1K , GLUE, ModelNet40, VQA\,v2 and NLVR2. The results demonstrate that a single learned interaction mechanism can recover the behavior of all three architectural families from data.
core_methodology: ITNet introduces a learnable integral transform that unifies convolutional networks, recurrent networks, and transformers by modeling pairwise interactions through a neural network kernel. This allows the model to adapt its behavior from data, potentially capturing complex patterns in financial time series.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources, but the methodology can be applied to market data such as price series, order book data, or alternative data like news sentiment.
alpha_potential: The unified architecture could capture diverse market signals (momentum, mean-reversion, event-driven) in a single model, potentially improving signal extraction and reducing model complexity. The ability to learn interactions between positions and features is particularly relevant for time-series forecasting and cross-asset modeling.
title_cn: ITNet：一种可学习的积分变换网络，统一卷积、注意力和循环机制
summary_cn: ITNet提出了一种可学习的积分变换网络，通过神经网络核统一了卷积、注意力和循环机制。这种架构能够自适应地从数据中学习位置和特征间的交互关系，在金融时间序列预测和多因子建模中具有潜在优势，可同时捕捉市场中的局部模式、长期依赖和跨资产关联。

title: How Good Can Linear Models Be for Time-Series Forecasting?
summary: Time-series forecasting research has been moving steadily toward larger architectures, from specialized transformers to general-purpose foundation models, on the assumption that capacity is what unlocks accuracy. We take the opposite position: most of the gap can be closed at far lower cost by tuning preprocessing rather than scaling models. We use Ridge regression as the testbed, since it has a closed-form solution and interpretable weights, which let the optimal hyperparameters be read off the search directly. We search over context length, local normalization, regularization, and augmentation on eight standard benchmarks and find three patterns.
